code: f <- function(x) jnp_sum(jnp_tanh(x)^2) make_jaxpr(f)(as_jax(c(1, 2, 3))) #> { lambda ; a:f32[3]. let #>     b:f32[3] = tanh a #>     c:f32[3] = integer_pow[y=2] b #>     d:f32[] = reduce_sum[axes=0] c #>   in (d) } make_jaxpr(grad(f))(as_jax(c(1, 2, 3))) #> { lambda ; a:f32[3]. let #>     b:f32[3] = tanh a #>     c:f32[3] = one_minus_square b #>     d:f32[3] = mul 2.0:f32[] b #>     e:f32[3] = broadcast_in_dim[shape=3 broadcast_dimensions=()] 1.0:f32[] #>     f:f32[3] = mul e d #>     g:f32[3] = mul f c #>   in (g) } cat(lower_text(f, as_jax(c(1, 2, 3)))) #> "builtin.module"() <{sym_name = "jit_fun"}> ({ #>   "func.func"() <{function_type = (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<f32>, sym_name = "main", sym_visibility = "public"}> ({ #>   ^bb0(%arg0: tensor<3xf32>): #>     %0 = "stablehlo.tanh"(%arg0) : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<3xf32> #>     %1 = "stablehlo.multiply"(%0, %0) : (tensor<3xf32>, tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<3xf32> #>     %2 = "stablehlo.constant"() <{value = dense<0x00000000> : tensor<f32>}> : () -> tensor<f32> #>     %6 = "stablehlo.reduce"(%1, %2) <{dimensions = array<i64: 0>}> ({ #>     ^bb0(%3: tensor<f32>, %4: tensor<f32>): #>       %5 = "stablehlo.add"(%3, %4) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> #>       "stablehlo.return"(%5) : (tensor<f32>) -> () #>     }) : (tensor<3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> #>     "func.return"(%6) : (tensor<f32>) -> () #>   }) : () -> () #> }) {mhlo.num_partitions = 1 : i32, mhlo.num_replicas = 1 : i32} : () -> () eval_shape(function(a, b) a %*% b, jnp_ones(c(2L, 3L)), jnp_ones(c(3L, 5L))) #> ShapedArray(f32[2,5]) jax_typeof(jnp_ones(c(2L, 3L))) #> ShapedArray(f32[2,3]) print_saved_residuals(function(x) jnp_sum(jnp_sin(x) * x), as_jax(c(1, 2))) #> f32[2] from the argument x #> f32[2] output of sin from unknown #> f32[2] output of cos from unknown

title: Callbacks, debugging, configuration and state
text: function made jit normally traces, lowers compiles first call. stages also available one time, jax.stages: f$trace(...) returns traced program, $lower() StableHLO module $compile() executable accepts exactly shapes dtypes compiled . f$lower(...) shortcut f$trace(...)$lower(), f$eval_shape(...) gives output shapes, f$clear_cache() drops compiled versions f holds.

title: Callbacks, debugging, configuration and state
text: pure_callback embeds R function side effects traced program. declare shape dtype result ShapeDtypeStruct. R function receives ordinary R vectors arrays returns R data (jaxR arrays). callback derivative . Give one custom_jvp: io_callback functions side effects (reading data, writing logs); ordered = TRUE calls run program order.
code: host_bessel <- function(x) besselJ(x, nu = 0) bessel_j0 <- function(x) {   pure_callback(host_bessel, ShapeDtypeStruct(dim(x), "float32"), x,                 vmap_method = "sequential") } jit(bessel_j0)(as_jax(c(0, 1, 2.5))) #> Array f32[3] #> [1]  1.00000000  0.76519769 -0.04838378 vmap(bessel_j0)(as_jax(matrix(c(0, 1, 2, 3), 2))) #> Array f32[2,2] #>           [,1]       [,2] #> [1,] 1.0000000  0.2238908 #> [2,] 0.7651977 -0.2600520 j0 <- custom_jvp(bessel_j0, jvp = function(primals, tangents) {   x <- primals[[1]]   d <- pure_callback(function(v) -besselJ(v, nu = 1),                      ShapeDtypeStruct(dim(x), "float32"), x, vmap_method = "sequential")   list(bessel_j0(x), d * tangents[[1]]) }) grad(function(x) jnp_sum(j0(x)))(as_jax(c(0.5, 1))) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -0.2422685 -0.4400506 log <- character(0) h <- jit(function(x) {   io_callback(function(v) { log <<- c(log, sprintf("saw %g", v)); v },               ShapeDtypeStruct(integer(0), "float32"), x, ordered = TRUE) }) invisible(h(as_jax(3))) log #> [1] "saw 3"

text: new_ref creates mutable box transformations understand (port jax.new_ref). Reads r[], writes r[] <- value; jit threads state compiled function. freeze(ref) returns final value invalidates reference. reference passed argument function vmap mapped value: call sees reference holding one element, afterwards reference holds stacked results. reference body lax_scan, lax_while_loop, lax_fori_loop branch lax_cond closes state operation: updated every iteration, holds final value afterwards. stateful random number generator vignette("random") built references.
code: counter <- new_ref(as_jax(0)) bump <- jit(function(x) { counter[] <- counter[] + x; counter[] }) bump(1) #> Array f32[] #> [1] 1 bump(5) #> Array f32[] #> [1] 6 counter[] #> Array f32[] #> [1] 6  # Local references make imperative accumulation differentiable poly <- function(x) {   acc <- new_ref(jnp_zeros_like(x))   for (k in 1:3) acc[] <- acc[] + x^k   jnp_sum(acc[]) } grad(poly)(as_jax(c(1, 2))) #> Array f32[2] #> [1]  6 17 totals <- new_ref(jnp_zeros(3L)) add_to <- function(total, x) { total[] <- total[] + jnp_sum(x); total[] } vmap(add_to)(totals, jnp_ones(c(3L, 4L))) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 4 4 4 totals[] #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 4 4 4 running <- new_ref(as_jax(0)) step <- function(carry, x) { running[] <- running[] + x; list(carry, running[]) } lax_scan(step, 0, jnp_arange(1, 5, dtype = "float32"))[[2L]] #> Array f32[4] #> [1]  1  3  6 10 running[] #> Array f32[] #> [1] 10

Optimizers: optimizers_sgd, optimizers_momentum, optimizers_nesterov, optimizers_adagrad, optimizers_rmsprop, optimizers_rmsprop_momentum, optimizers_adam, optimizers_adamax optimizers_sm3. step size number schedule (function step): Schedules: optimizers_constant, optimizers_exponential_decay, optimizers_inverse_time_decay, optimizers_polynomial_decay, optimizers_piecewise_constant optimizers_make_schedule. Gradient utilities: optimizers_optimizer() turns optimizer written single array one works pytree, exactly like @optimizer decorator, optimizers_unpack_optimizer_state() / optimizers_pack_optimizer_state() convert state plain pytree saving.
code: # Data from a noisy sine key <- random_key(7L) X <- random_uniform(key, c(128L, 1L), minval = -3, maxval = 3) y <- jnp_sin(X) + 0.1 * random_normal(random_fold_in(key, 1L), c(128L, 1L))  net <- stax_serial(stax_Dense(32L), stax_Tanh, stax_Dense(32L), stax_Tanh, stax_Dense(1L)) params <- net$init_fun(random_key(0L), c(-1L, 1L))[[2]] loss <- function(params, X, y) jnp_mean((net$apply_fun(params, X) - y)^2)  opt <- optimizers_adam(step_size = 0.01) state <- opt$init_fn(params)  step <- jit(function(i, state, X, y) {   g <- grad(loss)(opt$params_fn(state), X, y)   opt$update_fn(i, g, state) })  loss(params, X, y) #> Array f32[] #> [1] 1.115495 for (i in 0:299) state <- step(i, state, X, y) loss(opt$params_fn(state), X, y) #> Array f32[] #> [1] 0.008867357 sched <- optimizers_exponential_decay(0.1, decay_steps = 100, decay_rate = 0.5) sched(0) #> [1] 0.1 sched(200) #> [1] 0.025 pw <- optimizers_piecewise_constant(c(100L, 200L), c(0.1, 0.01, 0.001)) pw(150) #> Array f32[] #> [1] 0.01 opt2 <- optimizers_momentum(sched, mass = 0.9) g <- grad(loss)(params, X, y) optimizers_l2_norm(g) #> Array f32[] #> [1] 5.546106 optimizers_l2_norm(optimizers_clip_grads(g, 0.1)) #> Array f32[] #> [1] 0.09999999

code: loss <- function(p, x) jnp_sum((x %*% p$dense$w + p$dense$b)^2) * p$scale g <- grad(loss)(params, jnp_ones(c(4L, 2L))) str(lapply(g$dense, dim)) #> List of 2 #>  $ w: int [1:2] 2 3 #>  $ b: int 3 g$scale #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 48 batch <- list(a = jnp_reshape(jnp_arange(6, dtype = "float32"), c(3L, 2L)), b = as_jax(c(1, 2, 3))) vmap(function(el) jnp_sum(el$a) * el$b)(batch) #> Array f32[3] #> [1]  1 10 27  lax_fori_loop(0L, 3L, function(i, s) list(n = s$n + 1L, total = s$total + i),               list(n = 0L, total = 0L)) #> $n #> Array i32[] weak_type #> [1] 3 #>  #> $total #> Array i32[] #> [1] 3

title: Pytrees
text: S3 object leaf class registered. register_pytree_node takes class name, flatten function returning list(children =, aux =) unflatten function. list based class, register_dataclass shorter: name fields hold arrays fields static metadata. register_pytree_with_keys also records path entry child, register_static declares class leaves (configuration objects pass transformations untouched). register_pytree_node_class register_pytree_with_keys_class look methods tree_flatten.<class> tree_unflatten.<class> name.
code: new_gaussian <- function(mean, sd, label) {   structure(list(mean = mean, sd = sd, label = label), class = "gaussian") } register_pytree_node("gaussian",   function(x) list(children = list(x$mean, x$sd), aux = x$label),   function(aux, children) new_gaussian(children[[1]], children[[2]], aux))  d <- new_gaussian(as_jax(0), as_jax(1), "prior") tree_leaves(d) #> [[1]] #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 0 #>  #> [[2]] #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 1 nll <- function(d, x) -jnp_sum(scipy_stats_norm_logpdf(x, d$mean, d$sd)) g <- grad(nll)(d, as_jax(c(0.5, 1.5))) class(g) #> [1] "gaussian" g$mean #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] -2 register_dataclass("layer", data_fields = c("w", "b"), meta_fields = "activation") l <- structure(list(w = jnp_ones(2L), b = as_jax(0), activation = "relu"), class = "layer") vapply(tree_leaves_with_path(l), function(p) keystr(p[[1]]), "") #> [1] ".w" ".b"

text: Drawing twice one key gives numbers, rarely intended. option jax_debug_key_reuse (port jax.experimental.key_reuse), key random function used consumed, passing consumed key error class jax_key_reuse_error. random_split() consumes key returns new ones; random_fold_in() random_key_data() consume; random_clone() returns unconsumed copy. Indexing key array integers slices consumes keys selects; indexing adds axes (key[newaxis]), indexing integer logical arrays indexing traced indices pass state instead. check follows keys jit() (function consumes argument key closes consumes every call), checkpoint(), functions custom derivatives, lax_cond() (key consumed branch consumes ), vmap() (function mapped leading axis consumes keys uses) loops: lax_scan() lax_while_loop() body must make new key carry instead consuming carried one every iteration. Tracing alone (make_jaxpr(), eval_shape(), jit(f)$lower()) consumes nothing.
code: debug_key_reuse(TRUE, {   key <- random_key(0)   x <- random_normal(key)   tryCatch(random_normal(key), jax_key_reuse_error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)) }) #> [1] "Previously-consumed key passed to random_bits at index 0" debug_key_reuse(TRUE, {   body <- function(key, x) {     ks <- as.list(random_split(key))     list(ks[[1]], random_uniform(ks[[2]]))   }   ok <- lax_scan(body, random_key(1), NULL, length = 3L)[[2]]   bad <- tryCatch(lax_scan(function(k, x) list(k, random_uniform(k)), random_key(1), NULL,                            length = 3L),                   jax_key_reuse_error = function(e) conditionMessage(e))   list(ok = ok, bad = bad) }) #> $ok #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.4036463 0.8283720 0.5436133 #>  #> $bad #> [1] "scan body function leads to key reuse when repeatedly executed, because consumed inputs don't match sourced outputs"

title: Random numbers
text: Explicit keys recommended way draw random numbers, state visible. code translated NumPy also generator whose state updates implicitly: experimental_random_stateful_rng() (port jax.experimental.random.stateful_rng), style numpy.random.default_rng. holds key counter mutable reference; draw folds counter key adds one counter. size integer, integer vector, NULL broadcast shape parameters. rng$key() hands fresh explicit key (rng$key(4L) array keys), functions want one: generator works inside transformations. jit threads counter compiled function, repeated calls give new draws: vmap, split generator: rng$split(n) one generator holding n independent children, mapped call advances child. rng$spawn(n) returns children list separate generators instead. Without seed generator seeded R’s random number generator, set.seed() makes reproducible; inside transformed function seed required. counter reference, generator returned function compiled jit, carry lax_scan lax_while_loop; generator body closes works.
code: rng <- experimental_random_stateful_rng(42) rng$uniform() #> Array f32[] #> [1] 0.5302608 rng$uniform() #> Array f32[] #> [1] 0.7276642 rng$normal(loc = 10, scale = 2, size = 3L) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 10.864613 11.174528  7.716651 rng$integers(0L, 10L, size = 5L) #> Array i32[5] #> [1] 6 4 5 6 5 rng$random(c(2L, 2L)) #> Array f32[2,2] #>           [,1]      [,2] #> [1,] 0.7437396 0.5688519 #> [2,] 0.9454045 0.7802591 random_gamma(rng$key(), 2.5, 3L) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 1.0163749 0.6584333 2.8018618 rng$counter[] #> Array i32[] #> [1] 6 noisy <- jit(function(x) x + rng$normal(size = 2L)) noisy(jnp_zeros(2L)) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -0.2544037 -0.6385937 noisy(jnp_zeros(2L)) #> Array f32[2] #> [1]  0.288639694 -0.009632921 children <- rng$split(3L) vmap(function(r, x) x + r$uniform())(children, jnp_zeros(3L)) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.7198955 0.5716037 0.5674410 children$counter[] #> Array i32[3] #> [1] 1 1 1 kids <- rng$spawn(2L) kids[[1L]]$integers(10L, size = 2L) #> Array i32[2] #> [1] 9 7

text: distribution jax.scipy.stats provides functions JAX provides (logpdf/pdf logpmf/pmf, continuous distributions cdf, logcdf, sf, logsf, ppf, isf). Distributions available: bernoulli, beta, betabinom, binom, cauchy, chi2, dirichlet, expon, gamma, gennorm, geom, gumbel_l, gumbel_r, laplace, logistic, multinomial, multivariate_normal, nbinom, norm, pareto, poisson, t, truncnorm, uniform, vonmises wrapcauchy. log likelihood ordinary function, maximum likelihood needs grad: estimates converged, yet status 3 rather 0: single precision line search BFGS runs digits near optimum reports failure. JAX behaves way. Use enable_x64() convergence flag matters. observed information Hessian function:
code: x <- as_jax(c(-1, 0, 1.5)) scipy_stats_norm_logpdf(x, loc = 0, scale = 2) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] -1.737086 -1.612086 -1.893336 scipy_stats_norm_cdf(x) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.1586553 0.5000000 0.9331928 scipy_stats_norm_ppf(c(0.025, 0.975)) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -1.959964  1.959964 scipy_stats_gamma_logpdf(c(0.5, 2), a = 3, scale = 0.5) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -1.000000 -1.227411 scipy_stats_poisson_logpmf(0:3, mu = 2) #> Array f32[4] weak_type #> [1] -2.000000 -1.306853 -1.306853 -1.712318 scipy_stats_t_logpdf(x, df = 4) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] -1.5386882 -0.9808292 -2.0965471 scipy_stats_beta_cdf(c(0.2, 0.5), 2, 3) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] 0.1808 0.6875 y <- random_normal(random_key(1L), 200L) * 1.5 + 3 nll <- function(theta) {   -jnp_sum(scipy_stats_norm_logpdf(y, loc = theta[0], scale = jnp_exp(theta[1]))) } fit <- scipy_optimize_minimize(nll, as_jax(c(0, 0)), method = "BFGS") fit$x[0]              # mean #> Array f32[] #> [1] 3.200885 jnp_exp(fit$x[1])     # standard deviation #> Array f32[] #> [1] 1.611081 fit$status #> Array i32[] weak_type #> [1] 3 se <- jnp_sqrt(jnp_diag(jnp_linalg_inv(hessian(nll)(fit$x)))) se #> Array f32[2] #> [1] 0.11392063 0.05000025

code: A <- matrix(c(4, 1, 0, 1, 3, 0, 0, 0, 2), 3) a <- experimental_sparse_CSR$fromdense(A) rhs <- as_jax(c(1, 2, 3)) if (requireNamespace("Matrix", quietly = TRUE)) {   x <- experimental_sparse_linalg_spsolve(a$data, a$indices, a$indptr, rhs)   print(x)   print(grad(function(b) jnp_sum(     experimental_sparse_linalg_spsolve(a$data, a$indices, a$indptr, b)))(rhs)) } #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.09090909 0.63636363 1.50000000 #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.1818182 0.2727273 0.5000000 D <- jnp_diag(jnp_arange(20, dtype = "float32")) X0 <- jnp_reshape(jnp_sin(jnp_arange(40, dtype = "float32")), c(20L, 2L)) res <- experimental_sparse_linalg_lobpcg_standard(D, X0) res[[1]] #> Array f32[2] #> [1] 19 18 spd <- experimental_sparse_BCOO$fromdense(A) scipy_sparse_linalg_cg(function(u) spd %*% u, rhs)[[1]] #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.0909091 0.6363636 1.4999999

title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: transformation calls function tracers: stand-ins record operations applied . function must therefore written jaxR operations (jnp_*, lax_*, R operators) must pure: result depends arguments, side effects. make_jaxpr() shows recorded program. Ordinary R code depend array values runs trace time: loops fixed range, shape plain R value, calls R functions. R control flow array value work tracing, tracer value. Use jnp_where() structured control flow lax (lax_cond, lax_while_loop, lax_scan; see vignette("lax", package = "jaxR")).
code: f <- function(x) jnp_sum(jnp_sin(x) * x) make_jaxpr(f)(as_jax(c(1, 2, 3))) #> { lambda ; a:f32[3]. let #>     b:f32[3] = sin a #>     c:f32[3] = mul b a #>     d:f32[] = reduce_sum[axes=0] c #>   in (d) } poly <- function(x, coefs) {   out <- 0   for (cf in coefs) out <- out * x + cf     # an R loop, unrolled in the trace   out } make_jaxpr(function(x) poly(x, c(1, -2, 3)))(as_jax(2)) #> { lambda ; a:f32[]. let #>     b:f32[] = mul 0.0 a #>     c:f32[] = add b 1.0 #>     d:f32[] = mul c a #>     e:f32[] = add d -2.0 #>     f:f32[] = mul e a #>     g:f32[] = add f 3.0 #>   in (g) } relu_bad <- function(x) if (as.logical(x > 0)) x else 0 * x tryCatch(grad(relu_bad)(as_jax(1)), error = function(e) class(e)[1]) #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 1 relu <- function(x) jnp_where(x > 0, x, 0) grad(relu)(as_jax(1)) #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 1

title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: grad(f) returns gradient scalar valued function respect first argument. argnums selects arguments (0-based). several, result list. Arguments can nested lists arrays (pytrees); gradient structure. value_and_grad() returns value , has_aux = TRUE lets function return extra data differentiated. Gradients nest, higher derivatives need nothing new.
code: x <- as_jax(c(1, 2, 3)) grad(f)(x) #> Array f32[3] #> [1]  1.38177323  0.07700372 -2.82885742 loss <- function(w, b, x, y) jnp_mean((x %*% w + b - y)^2) w <- as_jax(c(0.5, -0.5)); b <- as_jax(0.1) X <- as_jax(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), 3, byrow = TRUE)); y <- as_jax(c(1, 0, 1)) grad(loss)(w, b, X, y) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -6.400000 -8.533334 grad(loss, argnums = c(0L, 1L))(w, b, X, y) #> [[1]] #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -6.400000 -8.533334 #>  #> [[2]] #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] -2.133333 loss2 <- function(params, x, y) jnp_mean((x %*% params$w + params$b - y)^2) grad(loss2)(list(w = w, b = b), X, y) #> $w #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -6.400000 -8.533334 #>  #> $b #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] -2.133333 value_and_grad(loss)(w, b, X, y) #> [[1]] #> Array f32[] #> [1] 1.36 #>  #> [[2]] #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -6.400000 -8.533334 with_aux <- function(w) {   r <- X %*% w - y   list(jnp_mean(r^2), list(residual = r)) } grad(with_aux, has_aux = TRUE)(w) #> [[1]] #> Array f32[2] #> [1] -7.000000 -9.333334 #>  #> [[2]] #> [[2]]$residual #> Array f32[3] #> [1] -1.5 -0.5 -1.5 g3 <- grad(grad(grad(function(x) x^4))) g3(as_jax(2))            # 24 x #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 48

title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: vjp(f, ...) returns value function maps output cotangent input cotangents (vector times Jacobian). Two options vjp() control computed kept. in_nzs marks inputs may nonzero tangent: others treated constants, vjp_fun$out_nzs tells outputs still depend marked input. saveable_args marks arguments may kept backward pass. argument array backward pass needs , marked FALSE, kept: vjp_fun$args_res shows NotSaveable() place, caller puts value back calling function (useful argument lives elsewhere anyway, held twice). Arguments backward pass need show NotNeeded().
code: r <- vjp(function(x) jnp_sin(x) * x, x) r[[1]] #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.841471 1.818595 0.423360 r[[2]](as_jax(c(1, 0, 0))) #> [[1]] #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 1.381773 0.000000 0.000000 a <- as_jax(2, "float32") b <- as_jax(3, "float32") r <- vjp(function(x, y) list(x * y, y), a, b, in_nzs = list(TRUE, FALSE)) r[[2]]$out_nzs #> [[1]] #> [1] TRUE #>  #> [[2]] #> [1] FALSE r <- vjp(function(x, y) x * y, a, b, saveable_args = list(TRUE, FALSE)) pullback <- r[[2]] pullback$args_res #> [[1]] #> Array f32[] #> [1] 2 #>  #> [[2]] #> NotSaveable() pullback$args_res[[2]] <- b pullback(as_jax(1, "float32")) #> [[1]] #> Array f32[] #> [1] 3 #>  #> [[2]] #> Array f32[] #> [1] 2

title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: custom_jvp() custom_vjp() replace derivative function, numerical stability differentiate iterative solver. custom_gradient() TensorFlow style shortcut lax_custom_root(), lax_custom_linear_solve() define implicit derivatives root finders linear solvers.
code: log1pexp <- custom_jvp(   function(x) jnp_log1p(jnp_exp(x)),   jvp = function(primals, tangents) {     x <- primals[[1]]     list(log1pexp(x), tangents[[1]] * (1 - 1 / (1 + jnp_exp(x))))   }) grad(log1pexp)(as_jax(100))     # the naive derivative overflows to NaN #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 1 grad(function(x) jnp_log1p(jnp_exp(x)))(as_jax(100)) #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] NaN clip_gradient <- custom_vjp(   function(x) x,   fwd = function(x) list(x, NULL),   bwd = function(res, g) list(jnp_clip(g, -1, 1))) grad(function(x) jnp_sum(clip_gradient(x) * 10))(x) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 1 1 1

title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: backward rule can send values backward pass. custom_vjp_defvjp_with_logs() (custom_gradient(with_logs = TRUE)) rule returns list(cotangents, logs), logs named list; with_logs method VJP function returns next cotangents, plain call drops . Log names must unique within one backward pass. rule defined custom_vjp_defvjp_with_accums() custom_gradient(with_accums = ) return cotangents: receives one gradient accumulator per argument pushes contributions . ValAccum sums acc$accum() receives, RefAccum exposes ref, acc$ref, indexed updates, argument differentiated gets NullAccum, ignores receives. suits rule whose cotangent sparse update large array. with_refs method VJP function chooses, per argument, whether gradient returned (ad_GradValue()), added ref (ref ) computed (ad_DontWant()); result holds GradRef() DidntWant() markers places.
code: scaled <- custom_gradient(function(x) {   list(3 * x, function(g) list(3 * g, list(incoming = g))) }, with_logs = TRUE) pullback <- vjp(scaled, as_jax(2))[[2]] pullback$with_logs(as_jax(5)) #> [[1]] #> [[1]][[1]] #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 15 #>  #>  #> [[2]] #> [[2]]$incoming #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 5 grad(scaled)(as_jax(2)) #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 3 pick <- custom_gradient(function(x, i) {   list(x[i], function(g, x_acc, i_acc) {     if (x_acc$kind == "RefAccum") x_acc$ref[i] <- x_acc$ref[i] + g     NULL   }) }, with_accums = list(ad_RefAccum, ad_ValAccum)) grad(function(x) pick(x, 2L) * 4)(jnp_arange(5, dtype = "float32")) #> Array f32[5] #> [1] 0 0 4 0 0 pullback <- vjp(function(x, y) x * y, as_jax(3), as_jax(4))[[2]] acc <- new_ref(as_jax(10, "float32")) pullback$with_refs(ad_DontWant(), acc)(as_jax(1)) #> [[1]] #> DidntWant() #>  #> [[2]] #> GradRef() acc[] #> Array f32[] #> [1] 13

what: Taylor mode: higher derivatives in one pass
title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: experimental_jet_jet() port jax.experimental.jet. jvp() pushes value one tangent function; experimental_jet_jet() pushes value whole truncated Taylor series, derivatives order 1 K along direction come one pass instead K nested calls grad() jvp(). arguments function, list arguments (point expansion) , argument, list higher order terms. series (1, 0, 0) scalar argument output terms first three derivatives: series (1, 0, ...) describes curve point, result Taylor expansion function along curve (Faà di Bruno’s formula). factorial_scaled = FALSE terms Taylor coefficients, derivatives divided factorial order. experimental_jet_jet() composes jit() vmap(). JAX rules arithmetic, elementary functions, linear structural operations, reductions, products, convolutions gathers; control flow primitives none, custom derivative rules ignored (function differentiated).
code: f <- function(x) jnp_sin(x) * jnp_exp(x) out <- experimental_jet_jet(f, list(0.4), list(list(1, 0, 0))) out[[1]]              # f(0.4) #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 0.5809439 out[[2]]              # f'(0.4), f''(0.4), f'''(0.4) #> [[1]] #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 1.955005 #>  #> [[2]] #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 2.748123 #>  #> [[3]] #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 1.586235 grad(grad(grad(f)))(0.4) #> Array f32[] weak_type #> [1] 1.586235

title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: vmap(f) maps f leading axis arguments without loop: batch axis pushed primitive. in_axes gives mapped axis argument (NULL argument mapped) out_axes places batch axis result. common use per example gradients: differentiate loss one example, map batch. Nested vmap gives pairs. axis_name names mapped axis collectives lax_psum() can reduce inside function.
code: dot <- function(a, b) jnp_sum(a * b) A <- as_jax(matrix(1:6, 2, byrow = TRUE), "float32") B <- as_jax(matrix(6:1, 2, byrow = TRUE), "float32") vmap(dot)(A, B) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] 28 28 vmap(dot, in_axes = list(0L, NULL))(A, as_jax(c(1, 1, 1))) #> Array f32[2] #> [1]  6 15 vmap(dot, in_axes = list(1L, 1L))(A, B) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 18 20 18 vmap(function(a) a * 2, out_axes = 1L)(A) #> Array f32[3,2] #>      [,1] [,2] #> [1,]    2    8 #> [2,]    4   10 #> [3,]    6   12 loss1 <- function(w, x, y) (jnp_sum(x * w) - y)^2 vmap(grad(loss1), in_axes = list(NULL, 0L, 0L))(w, X, y) #> Array f32[3,2] #>      [,1] [,2] #> [1,]   -3   -6 #> [2,]   -3   -4 #> [3,]  -15  -18 vmap(function(a) vmap(function(b) dot(a, b))(B))(A) #> Array f32[2,2] #>      [,1] [,2] #> [1,]   28   10 #> [2,]   73   28 vmap(function(v) v / lax_psum(v, "batch"), axis_name = "batch")(as_jax(c(1, 2, 5))) #> Array f32[3] #> [1] 0.125 0.250 0.625

title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: jit(f) traces f per combination argument shapes dtypes, compiles program XLA reuses executable afterwards. Arguments decide structure computation (shape, flag, function) must static: name static_argnums static_argnames. function recompiled new static value. traced value used concrete one needed; error says . Useful tools around compilation: disable_jit(code) runs code jit turned , debug ordinary R tools; log_compiles(code) reports compilation explain_cache_misses(code) explains function traced ; clear_caches() drops compiled executables; eval_shape(f, ...) computes shapes dtypes result without running f; lower_text(f, ...) returns StableHLO text lowered function; ensure_compile_time_eval(code) evaluates constant operations eagerly tracing.
code: selu <- function(x, alpha = 1.67, lambda = 1.05) lambda * jnp_where(x > 0, x, alpha * jnp_exp(x) - alpha) selu_jit <- jit(selu) big <- jnp_linspace(-3, 3, 1000000L) invisible(selu_jit(big))                 # first call compiles system.time(for (i in 1:20) block_until_ready(selu(big)))["elapsed"] #> elapsed  #>   1.702 system.time(for (i in 1:20) block_until_ready(selu_jit(big)))["elapsed"] #> elapsed  #>   0.765 make <- jit(function(x, n) jnp_reshape(x, c(n, -1L)), static_argnums = 1L) make(jnp_arange(6), 2L) #> Array i32[2,3] #>      [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,]    0    1    2 #> [2,]    3    4    5 make(jnp_arange(6), 3L) #> Array i32[3,2] #>      [,1] [,2] #> [1,]    0    1 #> [2,]    2    3 #> [3,]    4    5 bad <- jit(function(x, n) jnp_reshape(x, c(n, -1L))) tryCatch(bad(jnp_arange(6), 2L), error = function(e) class(e)[1:2]) #> [1] "jax_type_error" "jax_error" eval_shape(function(a, b) a %*% b, ShapeDtypeStruct(c(3L, 4L), "float32"), ShapeDtypeStruct(c(4L, 2L), "float32")) #> ShapedArray(f32[3,2]) cat(lower_text(function(x) x * 2 + 1, as_jax(c(1, 2)))) #> "builtin.module"() <{sym_name = "jit_fun"}> ({ #>   "func.func"() <{function_type = (tensor<2xf32>) -> tensor<2xf32>, sym_name = "main", sym_visibility = "public"}> ({ #>   ^bb0(%arg0: tensor<2xf32>): #>     %0 = "stablehlo.constant"() <{value = dense<0x40000000> : tensor<f32>}> : () -> tensor<f32> #>     %1 = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%0) <{broadcast_dimensions = array<i64>}> : (tensor<f32>) -> tensor<2xf32> #>     %2 = "stablehlo.multiply"(%arg0, %1) : (tensor<2xf32>, tensor<2xf32>) -> tensor<2xf32> #>     %3 = "stablehlo.constant"() <{value = dense<0x3F800000> : tensor<f32>}> : () -> tensor<f32> #>     %4 = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%3) <{broadcast_dimensions = array<i64>}> : (tensor<f32>) -> tensor<2xf32> #>     %5 = "stablehlo.add"(%2, %4) : (tensor<2xf32>, tensor<2xf32>) -> tensor<2xf32> #>     "func.return"(%5) : (tensor<2xf32>) -> () #>   }) : () -> () #> }) {mhlo.num_partitions = 1 : i32, mhlo.num_replicas = 1 : i32} : () -> ()

what: Ahead of time compilation, saved executables and the disk cache
title: Function transformations: grad, vmap and jit
text: jit(f)$lower(...) lowers f given arguments (ShapeDtypeStruct values) $compile() compiles ; compiled function accepts arguments shapes dtypes. jax.experimental.serialize_executable, compiled function can saved loaded later R session platform XLA runtime, without tracing compiling . persistent compilation cache automatically: cache directory set, every program whose compilation took least jax_persistent_cache_min_compile_time_secs seconds (default 1) written , later sessions read back instead compiling. jax_enable_compilation_cache = FALSE turns . cached file native code, use directory can write .
code: compiled <- jit(function(x) jnp_tanh(x) * 2)$lower(as_jax(c(0, 1)))$compile() s <- experimental_serialize_executable_serialize(compiled) path <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") saveRDS(s, path) s <- readRDS(path) loaded <- experimental_serialize_executable_deserialize_and_load(s[[1]], s[[2]], s[[3]]) loaded(as_jax(c(0.5, 2))) #> Array f32[2] #> [1] 0.9242343 1.9280552 experimental_compilation_cache_set_cache_dir(file.path(tempdir(), "jax_cache")) jax_config_update("jax_persistent_cache_min_compile_time_secs", 0) invisible(jit(function(x) jnp_cos(x) + 1)(as_jax(1))) length(list.files(file.path(tempdir(), "jax_cache"))) > 0 #> [1] TRUE jax_config_update("jax_compilation_cache_dir", NULL) jax_config_update("jax_persistent_cache_min_compile_time_secs", 1)

text: jaxR R mirror JAX: composable transformations array programs (grad, vmap, jit, jvp, vjp, linearize, jacfwd, jacrev, hessian, checkpoint), NumPy compatible array API, lax primitives structured control flow, counter based random numbers whose bits agree JAX exactly, SciPy style special functions, linear algebra FFTs. Like JAX, jaxR traces R functions intermediate representation (jaxpr), lowers StableHLO compiles XLA.
